neighbours.label: the point where a text explains the origin of a name ('hence its name', 'which is why it is called', 'it was named')
fire: The lake turns pink in summer because of algae, which is how it got its name.
Its leaves are shaped like a sword, thus its common name, swordfern.
Because the island was first sighted on Christmas Day, it was named Christmas Island.
The mineral glows under ultraviolet light, which explains its name, fluorite.
These cells mature in the bone marrow, which is why they are called B cells.
The pass is always windy, giving the village its name, Windgap.
The bird mimics the sound of a cat, hence the name catbird.
The river runs black with peat, so settlers called it the Black Water.
quiet: The lake turns pink in summer because of algae, which attracts many tourists.
Its leaves are shaped like a sword and grow in dense clumps.
Because the island was first sighted on Christmas Day, the crew held a feast.
The mineral glows under ultraviolet light, which makes it popular with collectors.
These cells mature in the bone marrow, which is why marrow transplants help.
The pass is always windy, so travelers carry warm coats.
The bird mimics the sound of a cat to scare away rivals.
The river runs black with peat, so settlers boiled the water.
